summary: Turn `apps/api/src/requests/` from a read-only vacation projection into a real inbox. Three new tables (Request, RequestMessage, RequestEvent) and one defaulted column (Organization.nextRequestNumber) arrive in one additive migration. The existing spec-10 vacation aggregation moves verbatim into a VacationRequestFeedService so it keeps one owner and cannot be regressed; the controller then composes two sources. New endpoints create a request under an Organization row lock that allocates a per-org number, run four status transitions and an edit and a reassignment under a Request row lock re-read with FOR UPDATE, and append an immutable RequestEvent inside each of those transactions. Overdue is computed on every read from neededBy, the status and the reading account's timezone — no column, no job. On the web the Requests page stops being capability-gated and becomes everyone's inbox: a scope control gated on view-all-requests, filters in the URL, the unchanged vacation section still gated on view-requests, a new-request modal and a new detail screen with a thread, a history and the action controls the caller may actually use. The sidebar row becomes unconditional and its badge counts what is waiting on the caller. No mail, no unauthenticated route, no scheduled job.

tasks.title: Schema and the one additive migration: Request, RequestMessage, RequestEvent, Organization.nextRequestNumber

migration.note: One migration for the run. Three CREATE TABLEs plus `ALTER TABLE "Organization" ADD COLUMN "nextRequestNumber" INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` — no rename, no drop, no new NOT NULL on an existing table without a default. Deploy order read from infra/deploy.sh, not from prose: `infra/migrate.sh` runs at infra/deploy.sh:184 (as a one-off ECS task on the NEW image, whose task definition is registered at :177) and the services are only rolled out by the `tf apply` at infra/deploy.sh:188. The schema is therefore live while the PREVIOUS code is still serving; three tables nothing references and one defaulted column are invisible to it. The migration step is skipped on a web-only deploy (the `grep -qx api` guard at :175), so the API must ship in the same deploy as the schema. Indexes exactly as the Data Model states: @@unique([organizationId, number]), @@index([organizationId, status]), @@index([organizationId, assigneeMembershipId, status]), @@index([organizationId, lastActivityAt]) on Request; @@index([requestId, createdAt]) on RequestMessage and RequestEvent. FK actions as specified: organizationId Cascade, projectId SetNull, requesterMembershipId Cascade, assigneeMembershipId SetNull, resolvedByAccountId SetNull, requestId Cascade on both children. No Prisma enum — type/accessKind/priority/status/assigneeKind/authorKind/actorKind/action are String columns, matching Project.status (apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:719) and Client.status (:763).

concurrency.lock: none in this task — the column is added with a default so no backfill and no lock beyond the ALTER itself

tasks.title: packages/validation: capabilities, the 30 REQUEST_MESSAGES strings, the field validators, the overdue rule and the default comparator
tasks.notes: Register `create-request` (admin/manager/user), `view-own-requests` (all four) and `view-all-requests` (admin/manager) in BOTH unions: the lowercase-dashed `MemberCapability` at packages/validation/src/index.ts:506 with a row in every one of the four blocks of CAPABILITY_MATRIX (:580), and the PascalCase `CreateRequest`/`ViewOwnRequests`/`ViewAllRequests` in `Capability` and `ROLE_CAPABILITIES` (packages/validation/src/roles.ts) with identical grants. `view-requests` keeps its exact current grants — do not touch its row. Authorization: `can()` (index.ts:691) indexes CAPABILITY_MATRIX directly and does NOT normalize, so every new call site must pass `normalizeRole(role)` (packages/validation/src/roles.ts) — the DB still holds `member`, which the raw matrix answers `false` for. `hasCapability()` already normalizes internally. REQUEST_MESSAGES ALREADY EXISTS at packages/validation/src/index.ts:1746 holding spec 09's vacation strings; add this spec's 30 keys to that same const (no key collides — verified) rather than renaming it, because a rename touches every vacation call site and this spec must not touch vacation. Add: the title rule (trim + whitespace collapse, 3-200), the type/accessKind pairing, priority, the ISO-date + not-before-today rule for neededBy, the assignee-kind rule (`member` only — `client` is rejected, not ignored: TC-01-UNIT-03), message body 1-5000, decline reason 1-1000, the overdue predicate (neededBy strictly before today in a given IANA timezone AND status in {open, answered}) and the default comparator of requirement 43.

tasks.title: API read paths: GET list and GET detail, plus extracting the spec-10 vacation feed into its own service

concurrency.lock: none — reads take no lock; `lastActivityAt` is the only field a read path may treat as volatile (requirement 32)

tasks.notes: Move `listRequests`/`buildBalances`/`toCard`/`compareRequests` out of apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts into VacationRequestFeedService WITHOUT changing a line of their behaviour, and register it in apps/api/src/app.module.ts beside the existing RequestsService entry (:142). AC-12 and TC-01-INT-20: every key and value type of a vacation row stays byte-identical, so the mapper moves file and nothing else. The list response is `{ requests, vacation?, counts }`; `vacation` is present ONLY for a caller holding `view-requests` (TC-01-INT-18 asserts the key is absent for a `user`, not that it is empty). Scope: `mine` (requester or addressee) is the default; `scope=all` requires `view-all-requests` and otherwise answers 403 `scopeForbidden` — the server is the gate, the missing control is a convenience. Every query filters on `session.organizationId`, a required argument with no default; the path orgId is checked by OrgScopeGuard (apps/api/src/auth/org-scope.guard.ts) and never used as a selector. Detail: a caller who is not party and lacks `view-all-requests` gets 404 with the same body as a non-existent id (TC-01-INT-19). Overdue is derived per read from the READING account's timezone — `Account.timezone` is nullable (apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:37), so fall back to 'UTC' exactly as apps/api/src/documents/envelope-completion.ts:360 does. `counts.waitingOnMe` is the non-terminal count where the caller is the addressee, computed org-wide and independent of the active filters, the way today's `pendingCount` is. Model the caller/party helpers on apps/api/src/kanban/kanban.shared.ts.

tasks.title: API writes: create (number under FOR UPDATE), edit, reassign

concurrency.lock: create: `SELECT "nextRequestNumber" FROM "Organization" WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE` inside prisma.$transaction, then insert the Request, the `created` event and the counter bump — the shape of apps/api/src/kanban/tasks.service.ts:157-166 and :211. patch/reassign: `SELECT id FROM "Request" WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE` and evaluate the actor and status guards against that read.
otherWriters: apps/api/src/vacation/vacation-requests.service.ts:83, :206, :340 (submit / review / cancel) — Organization row FOR UPDATE
apps/api/src/accrual/accrual.service.ts:74 (manual accrual run) — Organization row FOR UPDATE
apps/api/src/requests/request-transitions.service.ts (T5) and request-thread.service.ts (T5) — Request row FOR UPDATE; no code outside apps/api/src/requests/ writes a Request row

tasks.notes: Authorization uses `can(normalizeRole(caller.role), 'create-request')` — a raw `member` value answers false through the bare matrix. A `viewer` gets 403 `createForbidden` and no row is written (TC-01-INT-04). The addressee must be an ACTIVE membership of `session.organizationId`: another org's id answers 404 (never 403, so ids cannot be probed), a removed one answers 400 `assigneeInactive` (TC-01-INT-06). `assigneeKind` accepts only `member`; anything else, including `client` and a missing `assigneeMembershipId`, is 400 `assigneeInvalid`. An archived project is 400 `projectUnavailable`; FOR THE CROSS-ORG PROJECT the spec says both 400 and 404 in two places — see finding P1, do not guess. `number` is written once and is immutable; the `created` event is written in the same transaction, so a request without its creation event is unreachable. PATCH accepts title, description, priority, blocking, neededBy only, from the requester or an admin, only while open or answered: a terminal row is 409 `alreadyTerminal`, another actor is 403 `editForbidden`, and an attempt on type/accessKind/projectId/number/assignee is 400 `fieldImmutable`. Each edited field writes one `field_changed` event. Reassign requires `ViewAllRequests`, validates the new addressee exactly as creation does, and writes `assignee_changed` carrying both display names in oldLabel/newLabel — the device of apps/api/src/kanban/collaboration.service.ts:28, so the trail survives a removed member. Every write touches `lastActivityAt`. Validation bodies are `{ error: 'validation_error', fields: {…} }`, the shape at apps/api/src/clients/clients.service.ts:383, with every message read from REQUEST_MESSAGES — never inline.

tasks.title: API thread and the four transitions, each under a re-read row lock with its event

concurrency.lock: `SELECT id, status, "requesterMembershipId", "assigneeMembershipId", "answeredAt", "resolvedAt" FROM "Request" WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE` as the first statement of every transaction, with the actor and terminal guards evaluated against THAT read — never against a row loaded before the transaction
otherWriters: RequestMessage and RequestEvent are insert-only and have no update or delete path anywhere in the application

tasks.notes: Idempotence is by construction, not by a flag: the guard runs on the locked row, so a double-clicked Grant produces one `granted`, one `status_changed` event and one 409 `alreadyTerminal` (AC-6, TC-01-INT-09). `answered` is written by the addressee or an admin; `granted` by the REQUESTER or an admin and by nobody else, including the addressee and including a manager who is not the requester (403 `notYoursToGrant`); `declined` by the addressee or an admin; `cancelled` by the requester or an admin. Requirement 23 has no message row for a non-addressee's answer — see finding P3, do not invent one. A decline writes its 1-1000 character reason as a RequestMessage in the SAME transaction as the status, so a refusal cannot exist without an explanation (AC-7); an empty or over-long reason is 400 with no status change and no message. answeredAt is written on the first entry into `answered` only; resolvedAt and resolvedByAccountId on entry into a terminal status only; neither is ever rewritten. Every transition writes exactly one `status_changed` event with oldValue/newValue in the same transaction. A message may be posted only in `open` or `answered` — 409 `threadClosed` otherwise — by any party, is append-only with no edit and no delete path, writes a `message_posted` event and snapshots the author's display name into that event's newLabel so the thread renders after the author is removed. Every handler updates `lastActivityAt`.

tasks.title: Web: the Requests page becomes the inbox — scope, filters, states, the new-request modal, and the vacation section it must not regress

concurrency.lock: none — the page reads; the in-flight guard on submit is a UI concern and the server is the gate

tasks.notes: Delete the `if (!canView) router.replace(.../members)` redirect: the page now renders for every signed-in member regardless of role (requirement 37). The vacation section keeps requiring `view-requests` and MUST keep the existing cards, their actions and their test ids — `requests-card-{id}`, `requests-card-avatar-{id}`, `requests-card-member-name-{id}`, `requests-card-approve-{id}`, `requests-card-reject-{id}`, `requests-card-status-{id}`, `requests-card-reviewer-comment-{id}`, the reject modal and the in-place patch after an action — because e2e/tests/requests-page.spec.ts:140-171 runs unchanged as the regression witness (Backward Compatibility 3). Wrap them in `requests-vacation-section`. Filter state lives in the URL. Import every component from @ds; no hardcoded colour or size, tokens only (var(--sp-8), var(--fs-14), …). The submit control of the new-request modal is never disabled for validation — an invalid submission renders every field error and moves focus to the first invalid field (AC-10, TC-01-E2E-02); disabling is only the in-flight guard, released on success AND on failure. Validation messages come from REQUEST_MESSAGES and are re-run server-side; the client copy is a convenience. Controls a role cannot use are NOT RENDERED, never disabled: no `requests-new-btn` for a viewer, no `requests-scope-toggle` without view-all-requests, no vacation section without view-requests. Empty states use `emptyMine` unfiltered and `emptyFiltered` with a clear-filters control; the error banner keeps the last good list on screen behind it.

tasks.title: Web: the request detail screen — thread, history, actions, inactive-addressee banner

concurrency.lock: none — every action posts to a locked server handler; a 409 is rendered as an inline error and the row is reloaded

tasks.notes: A new route; nothing exists under apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/[requestId]. The thread and the history are two panels of one record and are rendered separately — a message appears in the history only as the fact that one was posted. In a terminal status the composer and every action control are ABSENT from the DOM, not disabled. Grant is drawn for the requester and for an admin only; Answer and Decline for the addressee and an admin; Cancel for the requester and an admin; Reassign for admin/manager. The inactive-addressee banner (`request-detail-assignee-inactive-banner`) sits above the actions when `assignee.inactive` is true and the status is unchanged — nothing is cancelled. Every mutating control shows an inline error and stays enabled on failure. @ds only; the decline reason and the composer are multi-line fields — see dsGaps.

tasks.title: Web: the sidebar Requests row becomes unconditional and its badge counts what is waiting on the caller
tasks.notes: Move the row out of the `can(role, 'view-requests')` branch at apps/web/src/layout/Sidebar.tsx:82 so it is drawn for every signed-in member; the no-dead-links rule holds by construction because the destination now opens for every role (requirement 37). The badge count becomes `counts.waitingOnMe` plus, for a holder of view-requests, the vacation `pendingCount` it shows today, and is absent at zero as it is today. requests-badge-context.tsx currently returns early for a caller without view-requests and fetches `?status=pending`; both must change — the fetch runs for every role and the status vocabulary is now the one in requirement 42 (see finding P2). e2e/tests/requests-page.spec.ts:135 expects the badge to read exactly '2' for a manager with two pending vacation requests and nothing addressed to them, and to disappear once both are reviewed; TC-01-E2E-11 expects 2 for an admin with two requests addressed to them and no vacation. Both must hold from one formula.

risks.mitigation: every new call site passes normalizeRole(role); TC-01-UNIT-06 checks the matrix and the API cases run against real memberships. Do not change can()'s signature — that is a cross-cutting edit no spec authorises here

risks.risk: Requirement 43's comparator and TC-01-UNIT-04's stated principle ('the terminal row sorts below every non-terminal one') agree only when the terminal row is not higher-priority than the non-terminal ones
risks.mitigation: implement requirement 43 literally — keys: blocking-and-non-terminal, overdue, priority desc, lastActivityAt desc — and write UNIT-04 with the terminal row at `normal` priority and the oldest lastActivityAt, which is the configuration the case describes. If a reviewer wants terminal-last as an explicit key, that is a spec change, not a code change

risks.risk: The create handler takes the Organization row lock, which four existing writers also take (member remove/restore, vacation submit/review/cancel, accrual)
risks.mitigation: the lock is held for the counter read and the insert only, inside one transaction, exactly as the vacation writers hold it. TC-01-INT-03 fires ten concurrent creates and asserts consecutive numbers; nothing in the create path makes an outbound call, so the lock cannot be held across I/O

risks.risk: counts.total is not defined by the spec — org-wide or matching the active filters
risks.mitigation: mirror today's semantics (totalCount is computed from the unfiltered set, apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts) so the badge and the counts are filter-independent, and say so in the code comment. Recorded as a note, not a blocker

risks.risk: type=vacation on the list endpoint has no stated effect on the requests[] array
risks.mitigation: treat it as a section selector: type=vacation returns an empty requests[] and the vacation block unchanged, type=access|question returns the vacation block unchanged and the filtered requests. Recorded as a note

risks.risk: AC-3 and Backward Compatibility 5, read literally, forbid requirements 37 and 38 and TC-01-E2E-10
risks.mitigation: read them as they are observed — INT-18, E2E-08 and E2E-10 — i.e. no role gains sight of pre-existing DATA (vacation rows, other people's requests). The page, the sidebar row and a caller's own requests are what this spec exists to add. Recorded as a note so review does not re-litigate it

risks.risk: Three findings (P1, P2, P3) are unresolved when this plan is written
risks.mitigation: each is isolated to one line of one task: P1 to the cross-org project branch in T4, P2 to the vacation section's filtering in T3/T6/T8, P3 to one message row and one refusal in T5. The rest of the plan stands whichever way they are settled
